engine: A variation of the day↔night canon (window.DayNight). The canon's single-edge seam cannot do a SYMMETRIC double-clip, so V5 supplies its own reveal: it builds the canon in mode:'manual', reveal:'opacity' (so the canon stacks day + night and hands us .dn__night), then OVERRIDES the night clip-path on each t with a centre-parting inset — inset(0 (1-t)*50% 0 (1-t)*50%). At t=0 the night is a hairline at the centre; at t=1 it is full. The evening is born at the centre and grows outward to both edges. A 2px centre seam line rides the parting and fades as the gap opens.
entry: DayNightCenterSeam.create(target, { dayMedia, nightMedia, labels?, onUpdate? }) -> { root, dn, set(t), get(), destroy }. set(t) is PURE (0=day, centre closed .. 1=evening, fully revealed). dn = the underlying canon instance.

seed.dialect_source: Saisei centre-seam split (both halves part from the centre), applied to the day/night pair.
seed.move: night.style.clipPath = 'inset(0 ' + (1-t)*50 + '% 0 ' + (1-t)*50 + '%)'  — symmetric double-clip; t=0 -> inset 50% 50% (hairline at centre), t=1 -> inset 0 (full). 2px centre seam fades opacity = (1-t).

canon_call.note: the canon stacks day+night; the night opacity is forced to 1 and the centre-parting clip-path is written by the composite on each t.

mapping.centre_parting: inset(0 (1-t)*50% 0 (1-t)*50%) on .dn__night — the symmetric double-clip the canon's single-edge seam does not do; supplied by the composite via set(t).
mapping.seam_fade: the 2px centre line opacity = (1-t): solid at t=0 (closed), gone at t=1 (fully open). It does not translate; the parting opens around it.
mapping.canon_role: manual + opacity only stacks the two layers and provides .dn__night + corner tags; the reveal is the composite's, not the canon's.
